Compare two within-host SFS objects

Source: R/sfs.R
compareSFS.Rd

Computes summary statistics and a chi-squared test for homogeneity between two WithinHostSFS objects (e.g., two hosts or two timepoints). A spectrum built before QC can be compared with one built after it only when every filter applied used maxFreq = 1; otherwise their caps differ and the function stops.

Usage

compareSFS(sfs1, sfs2)

Arguments

sfs1

A WithinHostSFS object.

sfs2

A WithinHostSFS object with the same breaks, folding, polarisation and maxFreq as sfs1.

Value

A named list with components:

chisq_stat

Chi-squared statistic, NA when no test is run.

chisq_p

Chi-squared p-value, NA when no test is run.

df

Degrees of freedom, NA when no test is run.

min_expected

Smallest expected count under homogeneity, or NA when either spectrum is empty or fewer than two bins remain, and no test is run.

chisq_approx_ok

TRUE when every expected count is at least 5, the condition under which chisq.test does not warn; NA alongside the other NA diagnostics when no test is run.

n1

Total variants in sfs1.

n2

Total variants in sfs2.

proportions1

Proportion in each bin, sfs1.

proportions2

Proportion in each bin, sfs2.

Details

The test compares raw variant counts in matching bins, so the two spectra must share their breaks, their folding, their polarisation and their QC frequency cap (the maxFreq slot), and neither may be bias-corrected: the counts of a corrected spectrum are rescaled and no longer multinomial. The function stops, naming the difference, when any of these does not hold. Bins where both spectra are empty are dropped, and when only two bins remain chisq.test applies Yates' continuity correction. No test is run, and the statistic, p-value and diagnostics are all NA, when either spectrum is empty or fewer than two bins hold variants. The chi-squared approximation is unreliable when an expected count falls below 5; instead of a warning, that condition is reported in chisq_approx_ok, and the p-value should then be read with caution.

Examples

data(example_whe)
whe1 <- example_whe
sfs1 <- buildSFS(whe1, genomeLength = 1000L)
sfs2 <- buildSFS(whe1, sampleIdx = 2L, genomeLength = 1000L)
compareSFS(sfs1, sfs2)
